alt: A funnel: the many details a story offers pass through an audit, and only a few chosen details come out, showing what the writer thinks matters. Some details are left out, and they may be the ones that would complicate the case. Evidence is effective when commentary explains it and sufficient when its quantity and quality support the reasoning.
caption: Selecting evidence is already part of the argument.

alt: Five questions asked of each candidate detail: is it relevant to the claim; what job does it do; where in the story is it; does it complicate the claim; and does the whole set cover every part of the claim. Each has a reason, such as "sufficiency depends on coverage, not count".
caption: Audit each detail for relevance, job, position and complication, then check coverage.

alt: A two-by-two grid. A broad claim or pattern with one detail is thin; with evidence from several places it is apt. A narrow point with one quotation can be apt; with many details it is repetitive. Below, quality means specific words, short embedded quotations and details that bear close reading.
caption: Match the amount of evidence to the size of the claim, and choose details that carry meaning.

alt: A loop between claim and evidence. You can start at either end. If the claim opens new questions, look for new evidence; if the evidence does not support the claim, revise the claim.
caption: Interpretation goes back and forth between claim and evidence.

after: ## Worked example 1: auditing evidence for a claim
alt: A coverage grid for a three-part claim about Montresor. Detail (a), from the opening, covers parts 1 and 2; (c), from the middle, and (e), from the ending, cover part 3. Detail (b) can qualify and (d) is set aside. Using (a), (c) and (e) covers every part from three positions.
caption: Sufficiency is coverage: every part of the claim, from more than one place.

after: ## Worked example 2: revising a claim when the evidence pushes back
alt: Two scales. For Widow Lamb the pan of tea is tipped a little in her favour; for Sir Anthony's steward Pike's thumb rests on the sugar-pan, making it seem heavier. The first claim, that Pike is honest, fails; the revised claim says his scales serve loyalty, giving to the poor what they take from the powerful.
caption: When the evidence pushes back, revise the claim to account for all of it.

alt: Four jobs, each with a stem and an example: illustrate with "The narrator shows ... when ...", exemplify with "One example is ...", amplify with "This is intensified when ...", and qualify with "Yet ..." or "Although ...".
caption: Choose a lead-in that matches the job the evidence is doing.
